stemMd:
A survey analyst argues that a district's larger number of reported problems does not necessarily mean a higher reporting rate among residents.

| District | Residents | Reports |
|---|---:|---:|
| North | 2,000 | 120 |
| South | 500 | 45 |

Which statement best illustrates the analyst's point?

options.label: A
options.textMd: Both districts have the same reports-per-resident rate.

options.label: B
options.textMd: North has fewer residents than South.

options.label: C
options.textMd: North has more reports, but South has 9 reports per 100 residents compared with North's 6.

options.label: D
options.textMd: South has more total reports than North.

explanationMd: Normalize reports by population: North is 120/2000=6 percent; South is 45/500=9 percent. The absolute count and population-adjusted rate rank the districts differently.

distractorRationale.b: North has four times as many residents.
